text: description: Use when writing or debugging a saved Claude Code Workflow (a .js/.mjs orchestration script under ~/.claude/workflows that uses the injected agent/parallel/phase globals to fan out subagents). Covers the exact runtime API, the args-as-string gotcha, the banned Date.now() non-determinism, worktree isolation for file-mutating agents, one-level nesting, a schema on every fan-in, null-tolerant barriers via filter(Boolean), per-work-unit pipelines so one slow agent cannot deadlock the cohort, cache-cliff-aware fan-out, the typed Codex output-schema landmine when MCP tools are active, and the SDK context-editing / task-budgets / canUseTool notes. Also the map to the saved schema-typed gate Workflows plan-gate and design-gate and the mechanical plan-lint stage-0. Triggers include author a workflow, write a saved workflow, fan out subagents, my parallel workflow deadlocks, workflow returns empty, schema-typed reviewers, or codify a gate as a workflow. NOT for single ad-hoc Task subagents (spawn a Task directly) or for the metaswarm phase pipeline itself.
A workflow file is NOT a plain ES module. The runner injects three globals —
`agent`, `parallel`, `phase` — reads your `export const meta`, wraps the body so
top-level `await` and a trailing top-level `return` are legal, and executes it.
effort: 'high',         // reasoning effort: 'low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh'
## 2. args-as-string (the recorded gotcha)
A Workflow receives its invocation arguments as **one single string**, not a
parsed array or object. If you expect structured input, **parse it yourself**
inside the workflow, and design for the common case where there is no reliable
arg channel at all: **have the agents auto-discover their input from live files**
(Read/Glob) rather than relying on args being threaded in. The saved gate
Workflows do exactly this — they tell each reviewer where to find the plan/design
doc and let it locate + Read it. Do not assume `argv[1]` semantics.

live_only_hunks.section: ## 7. One-level nesting + a schema on EVERY fan-in
text: - **Schema on every fan-in — but ARTIFACT-FIRST, and keep the schema SMALL.**
Every `agent()` that feeds an aggregation carries a `schema`, so you aggregate
typed objects instead of re-parsing prose. But the schema must be a *pointer*,
not the deliverable (see the artifact-first rule below).
**Do NOT set `additionalProperties: false` on a fan-in schema.** It converts a
cosmetic extra key into a hard, unrecoverable rejection, and it is the
difference between "one stray field ignored" and "5 retries burned, work lost".
Reserve it for tiny gate verdicts you fully control.
- **THE `{"raw": …}` DOUBLE-ENCODE FAILURE — observed 2026-07-23 (`wf_950ea2e9-e82`).**
A lens with 35 tool calls and genuinely good findings emitted
`StructuredOutput({"raw": "{\"lens\":\"…"})` — the whole object JSON-encoded
into a single string field — five times, identically, then died:
`StructuredOutput retry cap (5) exceeded — 5 failed calls with no valid output`.
This is a DIFFERENT mechanism from the over-broad-`required` case below: the
model had all the data and simply serialised it one level too deep. Because
`additionalProperties: false` + 6 `required` fields rejected `raw` outright, the
retry surfaced no partial credit and the agent never self-corrected.
Mitigations, in order of proven value:
1. **Artifact-first** (below) — makes the failure survivable at all.
2. Omit `additionalProperties: false`; keep `required` ≤ 4; drop `minItems`.
3. Keep every schema **flat** — no arrays-of-objects in a fan-in schema; long
prose belongs in the artifact, not in a string field.
4. Say it explicitly in the prompt: *"Return the object directly; never wrap it
in a `raw` key; never place JSON inside a string field."*
5. Last resort: `try { await agent(p,{schema}) } catch { await agent(p) }` and
parse the text — a schemaless retry cannot hit the cap.
- **ARTIFACT-FIRST IS THE PRIMARY CONTRACT (fan-out-contract C1), not a
belt-and-braces extra.** Any agent whose output matters MUST write its full
deliverable to a pinned path as its FIRST action (skeleton with every section
marked `UNKNOWN - not yet measured`), rewrite it at each milestone, and return
only `{ok, path, headline}`. Then a schema rejection costs a pointer, never the
work. Measured cost of ignoring this: 57 minutes of a 10-lens audit wave
discarded on a serialisation shape (`wf_950ea2e9-e82`, 2026-07-23).
session cut is not silently redone.

live_only_hunks.section: ## Quick checklist before saving a workflow
text: - [ ] a SMALL, FLAT `schema` on every `agent()` fan-in — `required` ≤ 4, no
`additionalProperties: false`, no `minItems`, no arrays-of-objects
- [ ] artifact-first: every agent writes its deliverable to a pinned path FIRST
and returns only `{ok, path, headline}` (a rejected digest must never lose work)
- [ ] every fan-in prompt says: return the object directly, never wrapped in `raw`,
never JSON-inside-a-string
